new_commodity_proposals.evidence: No commodity in any namespace claims it per the pre-resolve table, yet today's captures carry matching products, so it is stocked and priceable. The food is boneless beef chuck cut into 1-inch cubes, sold in the fresh beef case per lb: not ground-beef (different cut, different price), not a whole chuck roast (sold uncut, cheaper per lb), not a steak id. If the estate already prices this under a spelling like 'stew-beef' or 'beef-chuck-stew', alias it there rather than minting.

registrar_rulings.reason: No namespace prices raw cubed beef under any spelling: the only 'stew meat' string in the estate is commodities.json line 40087, where the canned 'beef-stew' commodity (label 'Canned Beef Stew', $0.1538/oz shelf-stable at Sam's Club) EXPLICITLY EXCLUDES 'stew\s+meat' - the estate already ruled the raw cut out of that id, so aliasing there would price a canned Dinty Moore meal as fresh beef. The nearest real-beef row, beef-chuck-roast ($6.64/lb; board product names are all whole roasts - 'Whole Beef Chuck Roll', 'Boneless Chuck Roast'), is the same animal cut but a different purchase: sold uncut and cheaper per lb than pre-cubed stew meat, so SAME FOOD, DIFFERENT FORM - a new id, not an alias. No 'stew-beef'/'beef-chuck-stew' spelling exists anywhere, recipe-commodities has zero stew hits, and the live feed has no price cell for beef-stew-meat (all its 'stew' cells are canned goods, soup mixes, and recipe names). Mint in the RECIPE namespace (recipe-board-everyday baseline + recipe-commodities.json, alongside beef-chuck-roast). REQUIRED follow-ups or the daily audit pages Brad: (1) commodity-dupe-allowlist.json pair beef-stew-meat|beef-stew, reason 'raw cubed beef vs canned prepared stew - beef-stew's own exclude list already separates them; prefix rule will re-flag otherwise'; (2) pair beef-stew-meat|beef-chuck-roast (and chuck-roast), reason 'same cut, whole-roast vs pre-cubed purchase at different $/lb'. Prescribe include ['beef\s+stew\s+meat', 'stew\s+meat'] with excludes at neighboring-commodity rigor, minimally: canned, dinty moore, soup, seasoning, mix, frozen (unless the fresh case is empty), pork, chicken, turkey, lamb, veal, kabob only if priced differently, dog/cat food, broth, gravy - build from beef-stew's ~40-pattern exclude block as the template. Separately, per the two-namespace rule: this ruling mints the ID only; the ingredient NAME 'stew meat' has no vocabulary row and needs its own row minted through the name gate, and its macros need a label transcription - both FDC hits offered are chicken and must not be used.

macro_cross_check.verdict: pass on protein, LOUD FLAG on carbs
macro_cross_check.detail: Protein is the sharp instrument and it agrees: 44.5 g against the source's 40 g with the noodles counted, +11%, inside the band, so the 2.5 lb of stew meat is the right portion. Calories and carbs do NOT agree and the reason is structural: the 1 lb of dry egg noodles alone carries 1742 cal and 323 g carbs, and the source's published 500 cal / 27 g carbs can only have been computed WITHOUT the noodle bed (drop the noodles and we land at 446 cal / 16 g carbs / 36.5 g protein, which brackets the source). This decides whether the recipe meets this run's conditions: counting the noodles it is 664 cal and 56 g carbs per serving, breaching both the 650 cal ceiling and the 35 g carb cap; not counting them it passes comfortably. I am not the gate for that, but nothing downstream should read the pass without reading this paragraph. Optional cream-of-mushroom soup is included in the with-noodles figures (+29 cal, +2.5 g carbs per serving).
